source.title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday

accepted.question_text: Let Q_n be the n-dimensional hypercube, let Q_n^k denote its set of k-dimensional subcubes, and let ex_k(n,d) be the maximum size of a family of k-subcubes that is Q_n^d-free, meaning that every d-dimensional subcube contains at least one k-subcube outside the family. Writing the limiting Turán density as π_k(d) = lim_{n→∞} ex_k(n,d) / |Q_n^k|, is it true that for d = 3 all nontrivial densities coincide, namely π_0(3) = π_1(3) = π_2(3) = 3/4?
accepted.context_brief: Turán densities in the hypercube

evidence.quote: We conjecture that for d = 3 the non-trivial Turán densities all agree. Conjecture 1.1. For 0 ≤ k ≤ 2, πk(3) = 3/4.

accepted.question_text: For the hypercube Turán density π_2(d), consider the case d = 3m + 2 with m ≥ 7. Is the exact value π_2(3m + 2) = 1 - 1/(m + 1)^3?
accepted.context_brief: Hypercube Turán density at dimension 3m+2

evidence.quote: The second construction is larger for m ≥ 7 but it would be interesting to know if there are other constructions that beat both of these. Question 1.2. Is π2(3m + 2) = 1 − 1/(m + 1)3 for m ≥ 7?

accepted.question_text: For each integer d ≥ 3, let r(d) be the smallest positive integer for which there exists a 1-factorization of the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d such that the union of any r(d) distinct 1-factors is connected. What is the value of r(d)?
accepted.context_brief: Connected unions in hypercube 1-factorizations

evidence.quote: Question 2.1 (Behague, [1]). For each d ∈ N with d ≥ 3, let r = r(d) be the minimal positive integer such that there exists a 1-factorization M of Qd where the union of any r distinct 1-factors is connected. What is the value of r(d)?

accepted.question_text: Let integers b ≥ a ≥ 2 be given, and let (A_i, B_i)_{i∈I} be a finite collection of pairs of finite sets such that |A_i| = a, |B_i| = b, and |A_i ∩ B_i| = 2 for every i, and such that A_i ∩ B_j is not contained in A_k ∩ B_k for all i ≠ j and all k. Must one have |I| ≤ Σ_{i=2}^a 2^{i-2} * C(a+b-2i, a-i)?
accepted.context_brief: Two Families Theorem generalization

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let b ≥ a ≥ 2 be integers and (Ai, Bi)i∈I be a collection of pairs of finite sets, indexed by a finite set I, with the following properties. 1. |Ai| = a, |Bi| = b and |Ai ∩ Bi| = 2 for all i ∈ I. 2. Ai ∩ Bj 6⊆ Ak ∩ Bk for all i, j, k ∈ I with i 6= j. Then |I| ≤ Σ_a_{i=2} 2^{i−2} (a+b−2i choose a−i).

accepted.question_text: Fix integers t and n with 4 ≤ t ≤ n. Let g_{K_t}(n) be the maximum size of a family of graphs on vertex set [n] such that the intersection of any two graphs in the family contains a copy of K_t. Is g_{K_t}(n) exactly 2^{(n choose 2) - (t choose 2)}? Equivalently, is the largest possible K_t-intersecting family always obtained by fixing one copy of K_t and taking all graphs that contain it?
accepted.context_brief: Clique-intersecting families of graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1. For all t, n ∈ N with 4 ≤ t ≤ n, gKt(n) = 2^((n choose 2)−(t choose 2)).

accepted.question_text: Let t ≥ 3, and let F be a family of graphs on vertex set [n] such that for every G, H in F, the intersection G ∩ H has chromatic number at least t. Must |F| be at most 2^{(n choose 2) - (t choose 2)}?
accepted.context_brief: Chromatic-intersecting graph families

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3. Let t ≥ 3. If F is a family of graphs on the vertex-set [n] such that for all G, H ∈ F, G ∩ H has chromatic number at least t, then |F| ≤ 2^((n choose 2)−(t choose 2)).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every t ≥ 3, any family F of labeled graphs on vertex set [n] whose pairwise intersections all have chromatic number at least t satisfies |F| ≤ 2^{(n choose 2) - c t^2}?
accepted.context_brief: Weak upper bound for chromatic-intersecting families

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that the following holds. Let t ≥ 3. If F ⊂ P(([n] choose 2)) is a family of labelled graphs on the vertex-set [n] such that for all G, H ∈ F, G ∩ H has chromatic number at least t, then |F| ≤ 2^((n choose 2)−ct2).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every n ≥ 4, the maximum size g_{P_3}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] in which any two graphs intersect in a copy of the 3-edge path P_3 satisfies g_{P_3}(n) ≤ (1 - c) 2^{(n choose 2) - 1}?
accepted.context_brief: Path-intersecting families of graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.5 (Alon, Spencer). There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that gP3(n) ≤ (1 − c)2^((n choose 2)−1) for all n ≥ 4.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist an integer t and an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every n, the maximum size g_{K_{t,t}}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] in which any two graphs intersect in a copy of the complete bipartite graph K_{t,t} satisfies g_{K_{t,t}}(n) ≤ (1 - c) 2^{(n choose 2) - 1}?
accepted.context_brief: Bipartite-intersecting families of graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.6. There exists t ∈ N and an absolute constant c > 0 such that gKt,t(n) ≤ (1 − c)2^((n choose 2)−1) for all n ∈ N.

accepted.question_text: If S is a subset of the integer lattice N^2 with the property that no three points of S lie on a common line, must the lower asymptotic density of S in [n]^2 vanish in the sense that lim inf_{n→∞} |S ∩ [n]^2| / n = 0?
accepted.context_brief: Infinite no-three-in-line problem

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. If S ⊆ N2 is such that no three points of S lie on a common line, then lim inf_{n→∞} |S ∩ [n]2| / n = 0.

accepted.question_text: Let T_n^k be the k-dimensional discrete torus, and color its vertices red and blue with exactly half of the vertices in each color. Let p_R be the probability that a random walk started from a uniformly random red vertex stays in the red class for at least two steps, and define p_B analogously for blue. For dimensions k ≥ 3, which pairs (x,y) in [0,1]^2 can occur as (p_R, p_B)? In particular, is the attainable region the convex hull of {(0,0)} together with the points (l/(2k), l^2/(2k)^2) and (l^2/(2k)^2, l/(2k)) for k ≤ l ≤ 2k?
accepted.context_brief: Two-step walk asymmetry on colored tori

evidence.quote: Our main question is: what happens for k ≥ 3? A tentative conjecture is that the answer is the convex hull of the set: {(0, 0)} ∪ {(l/(2k), l^2/(2k)^2) : k ≤ l ≤ 2k} ∪ {(l^2/(2k)^2, l/(2k)) : k ≤ l ≤ 2k}.

accepted.question_text: In the same equal-sized red-blue colorings of the k-dimensional discrete torus T_n^k, what are the possible analogous probability pairs for t-step random walks when t ≥ 3? In particular, even for k = 2, what is the correct description of these pairs?
accepted.context_brief: Longer-walk asymmetry on colored tori

evidence.quote: Another interesting generalisation is to consider the corresponding pairs of probabilities for t-step walks with t ≥ 3. Here, even the k = 2 case is open.

accepted.question_text: Whenever the natural numbers are finitely colored, must there exist an infinite sequence (y_n)_{n≥1} such that every finite sum a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + ··· + a_k y_k with each coefficient a_i in {1,2} and with a_1 = a_k = 1 has the same color?
accepted.context_brief: Partition regularity for restricted coefficient sums

evidence.quote: Question 7.1 ([5]). Suppose the natural numbers are coloured with finitely many colours. Must there exist a sequence (yn)∞_{n=1} such that every sum a1y1 + a2y2 + · · · + akyk with ai ∈ {1, 2} for all i and a1 = ak = 1, has the same colour?

accepted.question_text: Whenever the natural numbers are finitely colored, must there exist two infinite sets A and B of natural numbers such that the union {ab : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} ∪ {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is monochromatic?
accepted.context_brief: Monochromatic sums and products on infinite sets

evidence.quote: Question 7.2 (F. Richter, Ultramath 2022, Pisa.). Suppose the natural numbers are coloured with finitely many colours. Must there exist two infinite sets of natural numbers, A and B, such that the set {ab : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} ∪ {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is monochromatic?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a family of subsets of [n] that contains no induced diamond poset, meaning there do not exist four distinct sets A, B, C, D in F with A ⊂ B ∩ C, B ∪ C ⊂ D, C not contained in B, and B not contained in C. Assume moreover that F is maximal with respect to this property, so adding any set outside F creates an induced diamond. Must every such diamond-saturated family satisfy |F| = Ω(n)?
accepted.context_brief: Diamond-saturated families in the Boolean lattice

evidence.quote: Question 7.3 (Ferrara, Kay, Kramer, Martin, Reiniger, Smith and Sullivan, [3]). Let F be a family of subsets of [n] that does not contain a diamond as an induced poset ... Assume further that F is maximal with respect to the above condition ... Is it true that |F| = Ω(n)?

accepted.question_text: Suppose the edges of an n-vertex graph are properly edge-colored, so no two incident edges share a color. Can the entire edge set always be covered by O(n) rainbow paths, meaning paths that never repeat a color?
accepted.context_brief: Covering properly edge-colored graphs by rainbow paths

evidence.quote: Question 7.4 (Bonamy, Botler, Dross, Naia and Skokan, [1]). Suppose that the edges of an n-vertex graph are coloured in such a way that no two incident edges have the same colour. Can we always cover the edge-set of the graph with O(n) rainbow paths (meaning, paths that do not use the same colour twice)?

accepted.question_text: If the edges of the hypercube Q_n are colored red and blue, must there always exist a geodesic path between a pair of antipodal vertices with at most one color change? Equivalently, in every antipodal 2-coloring of the edges of Q_n, must there be a monochromatic geodesic between antipodal vertices?
accepted.context_brief: Antipodal geodesics with few color changes

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.1 (Leader and Long, [3]). Suppose the edges of the hypercube Qn are coloured with two colours, red and blue. Then there exists a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices, with at most one colour-change. Equivalently, if the edges are 2-coloured ‘antipodally’ ... there exists a monochromatic geodesic path between two antipodal vertices.

accepted.question_text: For every red-blue coloring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n, does there exist a path between some pair of antipodal vertices whose number of color changes is o(n)?
accepted.context_brief: Sublinear color changes on antipodal hypercube paths

evidence.quote: Question 8.2. Is it true that for every red-blue colouring of the edges of Qn, there exists a path between two antipodal vertices that changes colour o(n) times?

accepted.question_text: Among all edge colorings of the hypercube Q_n, how large can the average, over all antipodal pairs v and v̄, of the minimum number of color changes needed on a path from v to v̄ be? Equivalently, determine the maximum possible value of (1/2^n) Σ_{v∈Q_n} m(v), where m(v) is the minimum number of color changes on a path from v to its antipode.
accepted.context_brief: Average antipodal color-change complexity in Q_n

evidence.quote: Question 8.3. How large can be the minimum number of colour-changes on a path between a randomly chosen pair of antipodal vertices? In other words, determine the maximum (over all edge colourings of Qn) of the quantity: 1/2^n Σ_{v∈Qn} (the minimum number of colour changes on a v-to-v̄ path).

accepted.question_text: Fix k ∈ N. In every coloring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n with k + 1 colors, must there exist a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices that uses at most k color changes?
accepted.context_brief: Multicolor antipodal geodesics in Q_n

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.4. Let k ∈ N. In any k + 1-colouring of the edges of Qn, there exists a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices, with at most k colour-changes.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a convex body S in R^3 that fails the Kakeya rotation property, meaning that there is some convex S-Kakeya body K in R^3 containing congruent copies of S in every orientation, but not every two copies of S inside K can be continuously rotated into one another while remaining inside K?
accepted.context_brief: Kakeya rotation property in three dimensions

evidence.quote: Question 9.2. Is there a convex body S in R3 which does not have the Kakeya rotation property?

accepted.question_text: For dimensions d ≥ 3, are there convex bodies S in R^d other than line segments and d-dimensional balls that still have the Kakeya rotation property?
accepted.context_brief: Examples with the Kakeya rotation property

evidence.quote: Question 9.3. Are there convex bodies S in Rd with d ≥ 3 such that S is not a line segment or a d-dimensional ball, and S has the Kakeya rotation property?

accepted.question_text: Find further applications of Pinto’s alternative-compression idea: situations where no single compression operator is guaranteed to preserve the desired monotonicity in every case, but where bad behavior cannot occur simultaneously across a larger collection of compressions, allowing a compression proof to go through.
accepted.context_brief: Applications of alternative compressions

evidence.quote: Question 10.2. Find some more applications where this twist on the compression method can be used to rescue a compression proof. That is, arguments in which any single compression operator is not guaranteed to behave well in all situations, but where this bad behaviour cannot occur simultaneously for a larger collection of compressions.

accepted.question_text: For every integer k ≥ 1, does there exist an integer K such that the following modular statement holds for all r and all coefficients a_1, ..., a_k in Z/(2^r Z)? Let d ≤ r be the largest nonnegative integer such that 2^d divides Σ_{i∈I} a_i for some nonempty I ⊆ [k]. Must there be a K-coloring of Z/(2^r Z) such that every monochromatic solution x = (x_1, ..., x_k) to a_1 x_1 + ··· + a_k x_k = 0 satisfies 2^{r-d} dividing each x_i?
accepted.context_brief: Modular Rado boundedness

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.1. For any k ∈ N, there exists K ∈ N such that following holds. Suppose that a1, . . . , ak ∈ Z/(2^r Z), and let d ≤ r be the largest non-negative integer such that 2^d divides Σ_{i∈I} ai for some non-empty set I ⊆ [k]. Then there exists a K-colouring of Z/(2^r Z) such that all monochromatic solutions x = (x1, . . . , xk) to the equation a1x1 + · · · + akxk = 0 satisfy 2^{r−d} | xi for all i ∈ [k].

accepted.question_text: For every pair of positive integers k and n, does there exist a dimension d = d(k,n) such that whenever X is a Ramsey set of size at most n in some Euclidean space, every k-coloring of R^d contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X?
accepted.context_brief: Boundedness conjecture for Euclidean Ramsey sets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 12.1. For any k ∈ N and n ∈ N, there exists d = d(k, n) ∈ N such that, whenever X is a Ramsey set of size at most n in some Euclidean space, and Rd is k-coloured, there exists a monochromatic congruent copy of X.

accepted.question_text: Let g(n) be the minimum number of sets of the form E(K_{a,b}) × E(K_{c,d}) needed to partition E(K_n) × E(K_n), where E(K_{a,b}) and E(K_{c,d}) are edge sets of complete bipartite graphs. Is it true that g(n) = (4/5 + o(1)) n^2?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic partition number for E(K_n) × E(K_n)

evidence.quote: Question 13.1 ([2]). Is it true that g(n) = (4/5 + o(1)) n^2?

accepted.question_text: Let g̃(n) denote the minimum number of products of complete bipartite graphs needed so that every element of E(K_n) × E(K_n) belongs to an odd number of the chosen products. What are the values of g̃(n)?
accepted.context_brief: Odd covers of E(K_n) × E(K_n)

evidence.quote: Question 13.2. What are the values of g˜(n)?

accepted.question_text: Fix k > 3 and let P be a family of permutations of [n]. For each t, write m_{k,t}(n) for the minimum size of a family P that t-shatters every k-subset of [n]. Outside the three regimes already known in Theorem 14.2, are there any values of t for which the extremal order of growth of m_{k,t}(n) is in a different asymptotic regime than t, Θ(log log n), or Θ(log n)?
accepted.context_brief: Possible extra asymptotic regimes for partial shattering

evidence.quote: As before, the same three regimes appear, but it is unknown what happens to the size of P when t lies in the range [k + 1, 2(k − 1)!]. In particular, we have the following questions: • Are there any values of t for which the size of an extremal family is not in one of these three regimes?

accepted.question_text: In the same partial-shattering problem for permutations, for which values of t does the threshold occur at which the minimum size of a family that t-shatters every k-subset of [n] changes from order Θ(log log n) to order Θ(log n)?
accepted.context_brief: Transition point between log-log and log regimes

evidence.quote: In particular, we have the following questions: • If not, then for which t does the transition from Θ(log log n) to Θ(log n) occur?
